translation_notes: prefixes: RDFS->rdfs, XSD->xsd. RDF RETIRED from the draft: RDF.type becomes `a`, so a `@prefix rdf:` would go unused and falsify the island count.

the exact boundary the stratum is about, six times over: within each of the six per-component loops (Junction, Reservoir, Tank, Pipe, Pump, Valve), the run of `g.add((component_uri, ...))` calls sharing that subject, with no intervening control flow or unrelated statement, merges into one `+{ … ; … }`. Two places do NOT get folded into the surrounding run, deliberately: (1) Junctions -- the last unconditional add (elevation) is followed by `if junction_obj.demand_timeseries_list: if demand_obj.base_value is not None: g.add(... baseDemand ...)`, a triple nested inside two conditions that do not hold for every junction; merging it into the unconditional `;` block would assert `wdn:baseDemand` for junctions whose INP entry has no demand series or a null base value, which the original never does. Left as its own `+{ }` inside the (one-line, 0.4.0-legal) nested `if`. (2) Pipes -- `hasStartNode`/`hasEndNode` share `pipe_uri` with the first five triples, but `start_node_uri`/`end_node_uri` are computed by two statements sitting BETWEEN the two `.add()` runs in the original; folding them into a single `;` island would require hoisting that computation above the first block, which is a reorder INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2 forbids. Kept as two separate `+{ }` islands, in the original order. The same shape (compute intermediate URIs, then a second `+{ }`) recurs for Pumps and Valves.

`wdn_namespace`, `junction_uri`/`reservoir_uri`/.../`valve_uri` and every `*_node_uri` stay Python-side and interpolated ({wdn_namespace.Junction}, {junction_uri}, ...): `wdn_namespace` is `Namespace(<a URL computed at call time>)`, not a module-level constant importable as a prefix, and the subject/object URIs are themselves computed per loop iteration from f-strings over the WNTR object model -- there is no static IRI or project-level namespace import to lift into `@prefix`.
